title: Financial Resources and Wind-Down Planning
summary: Demonstrating that the firm will hold adequate capital and liquidity from launch, under stress and in an orderly wind-down.
contentGaps: Written as part of a programme: Aim and Purpose is the module's one-line description; audience, prior knowledge and core reading come from the programme

sections.Aim and Purpose: Demonstrating that the firm will hold adequate capital and liquidity from launch, under stress and in an orderly wind-down.
Learning Objectives: Calculate regulatory capital and liquidity requirements for the proposed business
Assess additional resources needed for risks and stressed scenarios
Design a credible wind-down plan and supporting financial projections
Syllabus: Initial capital and ongoing regulatory requirements
Internal capital and liquidity self-assessment for new firms
Wind-down plans: triggers, costs and timelines
Intended Audience: Founders, executives and directors of firms applying for a licence or new permissions
Compliance, risk, legal and finance staff preparing applications or variations
Advisers and project managers supporting authorisation, expansion or acquisition projects
sections.Useful Prior Knowledge and Experience: Some familiarity with financial services regulation or the firm's proposed business is helpful. No prior experience of an application is required.
Core Reading: Basel Committee, Core Principles for Effective Banking Supervision (2024)
IOSCO, Objectives and Principles of Securities Regulation (2017)
IMF, Good Supervision: Lessons from the Field (Working Paper WP/23/181, 2023)
